description:
## Reclassification

JMAP-x2gd.59 (P1) finds that ChatBackend's foundation methods —
`create_object` / `update_object` / `destroy_object` at
`crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs:296-328` — have skeletal
docs missing 5 critical implementer contracts (SetErrorType
selection, Some/None semantics for update_object, state-bump,
cascade, multi-field atomicity).

A 1-grep cross-walk of `jmap-mail-server` (the canonical
extension-server template) confirms the same gap is present
there. Specifically (`crate-jmap-mail-server/src/backend.rs:80-134`):

- `create_object` (mail-server): ~17 lines covering placeholder
  sentinels and singleton types. Missing: SetErrorType selection
  rules, state-bump contract, atomicity within multi-property creates.
- `update_object` (mail-server): 14 lines covering Some/None
  semantics. Missing: state-bump, cascade-on-foreign-key-mutation,
  atomicity.
- `destroy_object` (mail-server): 1 line, byte-identical
  thinness to chat-server. Missing: SetErrorType for not-found,
  cascade contract, state-bump, atomicity.

The canonical itself is below the contract bar JMAP-x2gd.59
proposes. Per workspace AGENTS.md "Canonical Templates":

> If you reshape an extension-server sibling in a way that
> diverges from this crate, change this crate first, then
> propagate to every other extension-server sibling in the
> same pass.

So fixing chat-server's docs in isolation is the wrong move —
it creates divergence from the canonical that the next
mail-server contributor would have to re-propagate.

## Scope of the workspace sweep

Eight extension-server crates carry the same trio:

| Crate | Status |
|---|---|
| jmap-mail-server | canonical, must be fixed first |
| jmap-chat-server | matches JMAP-x2gd.59 description verbatim |
| jmap-calendars-server | likely same shape, unaudited |
| jmap-contacts-server | likely same shape, unaudited |
| jmap-tasks-server | likely same shape, unaudited |
| jmap-filenode-server | likely same shape, unaudited |
| jmap-metadata-server | likely same shape, unaudited |
| jmap-sharing-server | likely same shape, unaudited |

(The seven non-canonical siblings each need a 1-grep verification
that their `create_object`/`update_object`/`destroy_object` are
indeed cookie-cut from the canonical's thin shape before propagating;
the canonical's thin shape is confirmed.)

## Precedent

This reclassification mirrors:
- **JMAP-x2gd.67** — reclassified 7 prior api-contract findings as
  workspace-canonical via mail-server cross-walk.
- **JMAP-x2gd.69** — reclassified JMAP-x2gd.64 (update_object
  Ok(None)-vs-Some ambiguity) as byte-identical to mail-server.

Both .67 and .69 stay open as workspace-sweep trackers; the
per-crate beads they cover stay open as their per-crate
manifestations.

## What this bead does NOT decide

It does not commit to the exact doc shape of the 5 contracts.
The bead description on JMAP-x2gd.59 sketches them; the eventual
fix may revise based on implementer feedback or downstream-fit
review. Adopt the shape JMAP-x2gd.59 proposes as a starting
point and refine during the canonical write.

## Recommendation

When this sweep is worked:
1. Audit the 7 non-canonical siblings' trios for their actual
   current shape (1-grep each).
2. Write the canonical doc on mail-server (the 5 contracts).
3. Propagate to all 7 non-canonical siblings in the same pass,
   adapted only for extension-specific cascade rules
   (chat-server's cascade list is documented separately in
   JMAP-x2gd.72/.73 — those go in apply_space_patch, not the
   foundation methods).
4. Close JMAP-x2gd.59 (and any analogous beads filed for the
   other siblings during the canonical-first reviews of those
   crates) when the propagation lands.

## Engineering basis

- chat-server backend.rs:296-328 read end-to-end (JMAP-x2gd.59).
- mail-server backend.rs:80-134 read end-to-end this bead (the
  cross-walk).
- Workspace AGENTS.md "Canonical Templates" propagation rule.
- Precedent: JMAP-x2gd.67, JMAP-x2gd.69.
title: Workspace-canonical reclassification of JMAP-x2gd.59: ChatBackend foundation methods doc gap is workspace-wide, not chat-server-local
